subject.title: [Feature]: Inbound media shared across all agents — no per-agent isolation

question: What should the canonical inbound-media isolation boundary be across agents and channels: account-scoped, agent/session-scoped, tenant-aware, explicit-share based, or a staged combination of those?
rationale: The current report is security-sensitive and any implementation will create a durable media storage, reference, access, and sharing contract that should not be inferred by automation from one proposed account-subdir shape.

options.title: Define Scoped Contract First
options.body: Choose the ownership model, compatibility behavior, and explicit sharing semantics before implementation changes storage and staging paths.

options.title: Start With Account Scoping
options.body: Implement the lower-friction account-based directory model now, accepting that non-1:1 account-to-agent and tenant-sharing cases may need follow-up work.

options.title: Defer Broad Core Change
options.body: Keep only narrower channel-specific slices active until a maintainer sponsors the cross-channel core media-isolation design.

recommendation.title: Define Scoped Contract First
recommendation.body: Choose the ownership model, compatibility behavior, and explicit sharing semantics before implementation changes storage and staging paths.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest current history on the media store and sandbox staging code and already reviewed this issue as the broad tracker.
